title: The kingdom within (II.1)
hookLine: the kingdom of God is within you
tomorrow: can a calm person really do more good than a smart one?

cards: A map app can drop a pin on almost anything: a taco truck, a friend's parked car, a seat in a stadium. In Luke's Gospel, some Pharisees ask Jesus when the kingdom of God will come, and he won't give them a pin.

It doesn't come in a way you can watch for, he says, and nobody will say look here, or look there. Not a building, not a border, not a date. Then comes the line the Imitation picks up to open book two.

teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "For lo, the kingdom of God is within you." The Imitation starts book two right there.
Turn to the Lord with your whole heart, it says, hold outward things more lightly, and you'll see the kingdom of God come within you. Some readers hear Luke's little word within as inside you.
Some hear among you, Jesus standing right there in the crowd. The Imitation leans on inside. Then a picture.
Christ often visits the inward person, the chapter says, and the visit brings sweet conversation, comfort, much peace, and a closeness it calls wonderful. A house with a guest.
And a warning that keeps it honest: don't lean your whole weight on people, even good and dear ones, because people change. Not because they're worthless.

teach.h: THE FLOOR THAT HOLDS IS FURTHER IN.
teach.b: Because the floor that holds is further in. Now look back at the week, because it was building to this door. Resisting at the start was guarding the entrance.
Bearing with others was making room. The cell was the quiet room itself. Everyone's sorrow and as if today cleared out false hopes and later-maybe plans.
Steady zeal kept the place swept.

teach.h: THE KINGDOM OF GOD IS WITHIN YOU.
teach.b: Book one was housekeeping. Book two opens the inner door, and says someone is already on the way.

how: Catholics read the Imitation of Christ as a book of spiritual reading, often a chapter at a time, and many pair it with quiet prayer, an examination of conscience or time before the Blessed Sacrament.

o: a faraway palace at the end of the world
a private feeling with nothing to do with others
God's reign, found by turning inward

games.q: the inner door — tap the pairs.
p: the kingdom of God is within you

s: in Luke, Jesus says the kingdom comes with signs you can watch for
he says nobody will say look here, or look there.
the Imitation opens book two with Luke's line
regnum Dei intra vos est: the kingdom of God is within you.
every reader takes 'within you' to mean inside you
some hear 'among you': Jesus standing in their midst. the Imitation leans on inside.

games.q: a friend says she'll start praying once she finds the right church, the right retreat, the right city. by Luke's line, where's the kingdom?
o: not over there; within, and right where she is.
at the right church, once she finally finds it.
far off, only at the end of time.
games.why: nobody will say look here, or look there, Jesus says. the Imitation reads it as a call to turn inward, wherever you are.

practice: Close your eyes and come inward in three steps: the sounds in the room, then your breath, then the quiet underneath it. Three steps, no hurry. When a thought pulls you back outside, turn in again, gently, without scolding yourself.
If you pray, you can rest on Luke's line: the kingdom of God is within you.

wordCard.voice: The kingdom within. Jesus's line in Luke, and the first words of book two of the Imitation: God's reign, found by turning inward.

orig.note: Latin, the first words of book two of the Imitation: the kingdom of God is within you.

carryVoice: The line to keep: within you, not over here and not over there. A week ends on a quiet door.

sources.q: For lo, the kingdom of God is within you.
